rationale: Contracted/shortened variant of ⲡⲉϩϣⲃⲣ-ⲥⲩⲅⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ. Same referent — the kinsman-soul whose intercession parallels the Living Soul's intercession for the catechumen. Documented in lines 9-10 of K.279 alongside the full form in line 2.

Likely Greek μνεία/μνῆσις 'remembrance, mention.' Appears at K.279 line 1 in opaque context; the chapter's structural theme of remembrance (ⲣ̄ⲡⲓⲙⲉⲩⲉ) for the deceased makes 'remembrance' the natural fit. Confidence low pending parallel attestations.
Conjunctive 3sg.m. on ⲥⲱⲡⲧ̄/ⲥⲃⲧⲉ 'prepare' (cf. accumulated ⲥⲉⲡⲧ 'due preparation'). Documents Lyc. spelling ⲥⲁⲡⲧⲉ for ⲥⲃⲧⲉ.

Lyc. nominalized ⲥⲁⲡⲥⲡ/ⲥⲟⲡⲥⲡ 'entreat, beseech.' Recurring on K.279 (lines 3, 4, 25) as the technical term for the kinsman-soul's intercessory petition — paralleling ⲧⲱⲃⲍ 'prayer' as the intercessory action that effects release. Lyc. ⲡⲉⲡ for ⲡⲥⲡ shows vowel insertion. Cf. accumulated ⲥⲟⲁⲡⲥⲧ̄ 'request/petition.'

Substantival form on ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲧⲛ 'be wide, spread out' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide/broad'). Used here as the technical eschatological-soteriological term: the 'broadening of soul' (lines 19, 26-28) is the released, expansive state contrasted with the constricted ⲗⲁⲓ̈ⲟ̄ⲉ 'diminishment' of the captive soul. Direct correspondence: width = freedom, narrowness = captivity.

Verbal idiom and substantival form: ⲣ̄- + ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'do the thought/memory' (already in glossary as ⲣ̄ⲡⲙⲉⲉⲩⲉ 'make remembrance'). Documents the Lyc. variants on K.279 (lines 15, 17) — the ecclesiastical commemoration through which the church raises the deceased catechumen's soul.

Compound ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲏⲓ̈ ('house') = 'house-dweller, member of the household.' Already attested in accumulated vocabulary as 'inhabitant.' Here at K.279 line 14 specifies the kinsman-class of catechumens (alongside catechumens m./f.) for whom the church makes remembrance.
